_comment: F-16A Block 10/15 Subsystems-discipline ground-truth / comparison values, companion to VnV/BrandtF16A/GroundTruth/f16a_ground_truth.json (the consolidated cross-discipline file: geometry/aerodynamics/propulsion/weights/tail_sizing) and f16a_geometry.json (raw Brandt geometry/gear inputs). Each block holds a Brandt-workbook / cited-textbook OUTPUT or comparison reference the future Subsystems framework code will be checked AGAINST -- these are NOT toolbox inputs (inputs live in examples/F16A/f16a_L{1,2,3}.json .subsystems). NEVER backfill a unit-test 'expected' value from anything in this file; the future subsystems comparison report (examples/F16A/subsystems_brandt_comparison.md, not yet built -- docs/subplans/09_subsystems.md Files to Create) is informational only, matching the standing rule already stated at the top of f16a_ground_truth.json.
_note_file_structure: JUDGMENT CALL (io agent, 2026-07-31) -- FLAGGED FOR COORDINATOR/CASEY SIGN-OFF: the consolidated f16a_ground_truth.json already holds one top-level block per existing discipline (geometry/aerodynamics/propulsion/weights/tail_sizing), each carrying at least one real Brandt figure. This file was created SEPARATELY instead of adding a 'subsystems' block there, per the io agent's explicit launch instructions (which named 'f16a_subsystems_ground_truth.json' as the example filename to use). Precedent exists both ways in this directory: f16a_geometry.json (raw Brandt geometry inputs) and f16a_ground_truth.json (consolidated outputs) already coexist as two separate files, so a third, narrowly-scoped file is not unprecedented -- but two of this file's three content areas (fuel_volume, avionics_volume) are pure 'NOT MODELED' placeholders with zero Brandt figures, unlike every block in the consolidated file. If the coordinator prefers one-file consolidation, merge this file's 'subsystems' key wholesale into f16a_ground_truth.json -- nothing here depends on standing alone.
_source: docs/subplans/09_subsystems.md 'Ground Truth' section (Casey-approved 2026-07-31); VnV/BrandtF16A/GroundTruth/f16a_geometry.json 'gear' block (carried forward here with its caveats, not re-derived or corrected); VnV/BrandtF16A/todo.md, 2026-07-31 entry 'Subsystems deep-dive, Phase A (documentation): gear block provenance and implied gear-load-split'.

fuel_volume._note: No Brandt fuel-VOLUME ground truth exists anywhere in VnV/BrandtF16A/GroundTruth/*.json (confirmed 2026-07-31 during the scribe pass, docs/subplans/09_subsystems.md 'Ground Truth'). f16a_ground_truth.json's .weights.summary.fuel (value 6296.30 lb, Brandt Wt!B6) and .weights.di_reference_values are Brandt fuel WEIGHT figures, not volumes -- do NOT repurpose them as a volume comparison target (converting them would require the same uncited fuel density this discipline's f16a_L3.json systems.V_t._TODO_V_t already flags as an open gap on the weights side). The future subsystems comparison report should carry this as a gap row, not a full agreement check, matching how other reports handle Brandt components with no framework analog.

avionics_volume._note: No Brandt avionics-VOLUME ground truth exists anywhere in VnV/BrandtF16A/GroundTruth/*.json (confirmed 2026-07-31). f16a_ground_truth.json's .weights.engine_and_systems.avionics (value 2541.54 lb, Brandt Wt!B30 = 0.081*W_TO) is a Brandt avionics WEIGHT, not a volume -- and it uses a DIFFERENT weight fraction (0.081) than this discipline's own F-16 pick (examples/F16A/f16a_L2.json .subsystems.avionics.weight_fraction = 0.055, from a different textbook -- Raymer Table 11.6 -- than whatever produced Brandt's 0.081). Do not conflate the two fractions or treat one as validating the other. Comparison report gap row, not an agreement check.

landing_gear_tire_diameter._source: VnV/BrandtF16A/GroundTruth/f16a_geometry.json 'gear' block, carried forward VERBATIM here as a comparison-report data point for the new Raymer Table 11.1 statistical tire-sizing formula (examples/F16A/f16a_L2.json .subsystems.landing_gear.tire_sizing). NOT re-derived, NOT 'corrected' here -- both caveats below are carried forward exactly as logged in VnV/BrandtF16A/todo.md, per the io agent's explicit launch instructions.
landing_gear_tire_diameter._caveat_1_undocumented_provenance: This block's ONLY citation anywhere in VnV/BrandtF16A is f16a_geometry.json's own top-level 'gear' object '_source': 'Gear tab -- landing gear geometry' -- no cell letter/number at all, unlike every other block in that file. readme_geom.md's own Input Schema (Sec. 2), which is supposed to be the complete list of f16a_geometry.json input regions, and GroundTruth/cell-map.md both OMIT this block entirely (grepped for 'gear'/'tire'/'Gear', zero matches in either file). The block IS consumed live by BrandtBalanceStabControl.m:211-221 (x_nose/x_main/y_main/h_main only -- the two tire diameters d_nose_ft/d_main_ft are read by NO .m file in this repo). Logged: VnV/BrandtF16A/todo.md, 2026-07-31 entry 'Subsystems deep-dive, Phase A ... gear block provenance and implied gear-load-split', Finding 1.
landing_gear_tire_diameter._caveat_2_load_split_contradiction: This block's x_nose_ft/x_main_ft/y_main_ft/h_main_ft feed BrandtBalanceStabControl.m's gear_main_pct/gear_nose_pct computation (readme_bsc.md 'Gear load split' equation, %W_main = 100*(x_cg-x_nose)/(x_main-x_nose)), which returns 26.7% main / 73.3% nose for the F-16 -- a near-complete REVERSAL of both Raymer's stated typical fighter split (90% main / 10% nose, Ch. 11 p.344 prose) and Nicolai & Carichner's own repo-documented 'nose gear ~20% of TOGW' rule of thumb (docs/reference_extracts/08_fuselage_sizing.md Sec. 8.1.7, p.202: 'Nose gear rule of thumb: 20% of TOGW on the nose wheel for good steering'). NOT adjudicated here -- logged: VnV/BrandtF16A/todo.md, 2026-07-31 entry, Finding 2. The framework's own F16LandingGearL2/L3 classes use Raymer's 90%/10% default instead (examples/F16A/f16a_L2.json / f16a_L3.json .subsystems.landing_gear.gear_load_split), deliberately NOT wired to this Brandt-derived 26.7%/73.3% split.
landing_gear_tire_diameter._comparison_note: d_nose_ft=1.5 (18 in) / d_main_ft=2.0 (24 in) are usable as an INFORMATIONAL comparison-report data point for the framework's Raymer-statistical tire-diameter prediction, but -- given both caveats above -- NOT as a silently-trusted validation target. No T.O. 1F-16A-1 data was found anywhere in this repo (temp_Casey or elsewhere) giving an independent tire/gear dimension (docs/subplans/09_subsystems.md 'Ground Truth', final paragraph) -- this Brandt figure is the only in-repo candidate, and it carries the two caveats above.

gear_load_split_comparison._note: Recorded for the comparison report's convenience -- all three rows below are the SAME open question as landing_gear_tire_diameter._caveat_2_load_split_contradiction above, not new/independent figures.

brandt_derived._source: BrandtBalanceStabControl.m gear_main_pct/gear_nose_pct off the uncross-checked gear block above; readme_bsc.md 'Gear load split' equation and its own stated validation target ('Gear split about 26.7% main / 73.3% nose').

raymer_typical._source: [Raymer 6th ed. Ch. 11, p.344, prose]. Used as the framework's F16LandingGearL2/L3 default -- examples/F16A/f16a_L2.json and f16a_L3.json .subsystems.landing_gear.gear_load_split.

nicolai_rule_of_thumb._source: [Nicolai & Carichner, p.202]: 'Nose gear rule of thumb: 20% of TOGW on the nose wheel for good steering.' docs/reference_extracts/08_fuselage_sizing.md Sec. 8.1.7.
